L264@P2: puts all data in a single table of size p, instead of using multiple
L265@P2: independent tables. We use n independent hash functions capable
L266@P2: of mapping xi uniformly and randomly into any of the p locations
L267@P2: in the table. (Discussion on how parameters are selected is deferred

L269@P2: the table can store at any one of (up to) n possible locations:

L317@P3: find a "nest" for every credential by calculating the locations for the

L320@P3: or updating an account, is simply a matter or writing shares of the

L322@P3: Parameters. We select the default parameters for our cuckoo hash
L323@P3: table for a reasonable balance of storage costs and minimal probability of collisions. Each location in the table can only hold one
L324@P3: item. With n = 2, the effective load factor is less than 0.5. At higher

L346@P3: A 2007 study [15] on the number of accounts owned by the typical user found that the average user as 6.5 passwords, which are
L347@P3: shared between 3.9 different sites, and that each user has about 25

L357@P3: The overriding designs goal of the client is to minimize exposure of
L358@P3: user credentials to a small, auditable component. Hence, the client
L359@P3: is divided into two components: a trusted core that needs access to
L360@P3: the master password and sensitive credentials, and an untrusted
L361@P3: UI component that manages interactions with the webpage but
L362@P3: cannot access any Firefox API. The core and UI components are
L363@P3: completely isolated from each other and can only communicate
L364@P3: through the message-passing. For all sensitive computation, The
L365@P3: core component creates a NodeJS subprocess which uses its crypto
L366@P3: library for all cryptographic algorithms[39], as well as AWS and
L367@P3: Azure APIs for making requests to keystores.
L368@P3: Next, we describe how to setup the client, and what happens
L369@P3: when it is used in the brower to process a login request. Figure 1
L370@P3: illustrates the interactions between the user, browser add-on, and
L371@P3: keystores.
L372@P3: Setup. To use Horcrux users need to set up servers that store
L373@P3: shares of the users passwords. Our prototype add-on prompts users
L374@P3: to create accounts on AWS or Azure and create access keys with
L375@P3: permissions to use their noSQL keystores (AWS DynamoDB or
L376@P3: Azure Table Storage) in a specific datacenter region. More paranoid
L377@P3: users will configure keystores themselves using trusted services and
L378@P3: spread across jurisdictions. A user may also use their own servers

L238: ### III-D Compatible Boundary Changes
L239: Preserving external meaning. A losing verdict motivates a repair only if the changed boundary preserves the same problem. Candidate $\Delta$ may change modeled provider behavior or the interface, but not the policy or external specification. It yields $\mathcal{C}\oplus\Delta=\langle P_{\Delta},I_{\Delta},\varphi_{\rm app},\mathbf{W}_{\Delta}\rangle$ and a mapping $\iota_{\Delta}:W_{P}\to W_{P}^{\Delta}$.
L240: $\mathsf{PreservesExternalContract}$ requires $\iota_{\Delta}$ to be a bijection preserving the request, principal, initial authority, authorization choices, completion goal, $W_{A}$ membership, and the claim template attached to each response. In particular, $\Xi_{\Delta}(\iota_{\Delta}(w))=\Xi(w)$ for every $w\in W_{A}$.
L241: A candidate remains within $\kappa$ only while it stays inside the recorded contract boundary. It may refine internal state, install an eligible control or new $\beta_{\Delta}$, and delay success within the declared schedule bound, but it must re-establish the same public templates. The checker requires an exact match; one claim kind cannot replace another. Stronger enforcement is allowed, but a different public claim defines a different contract.
L242: The candidate must also preserve the projected effects and their meaning under $\eta$. It may add internal state or evidence and make an effect unreachable, but cannot erase a projected field, relabel an external consequence, or change how $\varphi_{\rm app}$ interprets it. Reachability may change, but effect meaning may not.
L243: These restrictions prevent redefinition: workload preservation excludes refusal, claim-template preservation excludes changing the public contract, and effect preservation excludes hiding a forbidden consequence. A new observation or control may change the preventive choices leading to $F$, but not the external consequence judged by $\varphi_{\rm app}$.
L244: Search and minimality. Given a declared repair set $\mathcal{B}$ and cost order, EffectBound evaluates the combinations that $\mathcal{B}$ permits and reports each Pareto-minimal repair (one not dominated under that order), or NoRepairFound when the declared repair set contains no winning candidate. Minimality is relative to the finite contract, repair set, bounds, and declared cost order. The set may contain the Bind, Re-enter, and Fence placements, as well as other declared changes.
L245: EffectBound then validates these candidates and connects the repaired contract to deployment traces.
L246: ## IV EffectBound
L247: 
L248: EffectBound proceeds in three stages (Figure 【60†3】): construct an analysis contract from provider evidence, check its verdict and any repair, and validate deployment traces.
L249: ### IV-A Grounding the Contract
L250: Contract inputs. A contract records provider behavior and interface, policy and workload, effect frontier, authorization origins and continuation links, claims, exclusions, and repair candidates. Schemas alone do not determine when targets resolve, whether operations are atomic, or how retries behave or requests fan out. Documentation, pinned source, controlled execution, or instrumentation must support those details. EffectBound checks the resulting contract, but it does not discover provider paths.
L251: Tracing authorization to effects. For every represented path, the analyst follows $g\to a\to c$ toward a proposed model boundary $B$, then asks whether any carrier can reach the evidence-supported effect frontier $F$. The analyst asks where authority is bound, whether an earlier check remains valid, and whether in-flight work can continue. Tests exercise late resolution, mutation, queues, redelivery, restart, and membership changes.
L252: The evidence record identifies the source and hash for each path, exclusion, frontier, and response meaning. Validation rejects missing evidence or hash mismatches.
L253: Fail-closed validation. A response either makes a closure claim or abstains from making one. Unsupported results when authorization origins, continuation links, or declared exclusions lack evidence, or when coverage of hidden behavior or exposed controls is incomplete. The Kafka trace for one authorized request continues beyond the proposed Kafka convergence boundary $B_{\rm applied}$ to the append frontier $F_{\rm append}$, so grounding rejects that contract before solving.
L254: Validation fails closed when represented premises lack support. It cannot detect a provider path absent from both the evidence inventory and the contract.
L255: ### IV-B Checking Verdicts and Repairs
L256: Verdicts and assurance. A grounded contract yields a checked winning strategy or losing certificate. Lean validates all 17 published source-to-game translations and finite-game certificates. Four NATS purge contracts—base, Bind, native-terminal (zero counters treated as terminal), and Tracked Drain (awaiting tracked callback completion)—declare the same instance-effect-closure requirement.
L257: For these four, Lean checks carrier-link well-formedness and derives each result from the materialized issuance, carrier, frontier-crossing suffix, permission, application-policy, and coverage relations. The compiler and solver need not be trusted after the finite contract is constructed (Table 【61†I】).
L258: TABLE I: Assurance boundary. Lean consumes, but does not infer, provider semantics.
L259: Material  | Status
L260: --- | ---
L261: Policy, authorization scope, workload, claim kind/subject, exclusions, repair set  | Analyst-authored
L262: Boundary/frontier; authorization links/effect paths; recorded safety/policy verdicts; scope/configuration match flags; scoped issuance/carrier coverage; post-settlement relation/invariant  | Grounded/materialized input

L265: Why analysis precedes repair. Testing one Fence cannot decide whether another strategy over $I$ works. Safety, truthful claims, and completion rule out denying everything. A losing certificate has $q_{0}\in L\subseteq Q\setminus G$. Every action available at an admissible $q\in L$ has an admitted successor in $L$. Grounding yields Unsupported when required premises lack evidence.
L266: Candidate checking rejects changes that block required work, reuse an outdated configuration version, or alter claims or effect semantics. The analysis thus separates insufficient grounding from missing boundary power before checking Bind, Re-enter, or Fence candidates from the declared repair set.

L569: An instantiation MUST support durable obligations and attempt duties with signed creation, assignment and status records. A duty is created from a recorded operation and its receipt, by an administrative session record, and carries its identifier, source intent, causal receipt, durable role, tenure, description, deadline, status, beneficiary, terms commitment, current performance assignee, optional succession rule and transition policies.
L570: Statuses are OPEN, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, DISPUTED, DISCHARGED and IMPOSSIBLE_OR_ESCALATED; a status change and a performance assignment are each signed administrative records. L571: ### 【92†8.2.】 【93†Succession and handover】
L572: 
L573: When a predecessor is terminated under a succession rule, the writer MUST provide a specified atomic handover operation; profiles MUST define crash recovery and the visibility of intermediate prefixes, since two adjacent valid events alone do not prove atomic storage. 【351†Table 13】 states what MUST hold across a handover.【352†¶】
L574: 【353†Table 13】: 【354†Handover rules】
L575: What  | Across a handover
L576: --- | ---
L577: Open duties under the applied rule  | Belong to the role; stay OPEN and are reported as surviving until the successor records a signed performance assignment
L578: Grants  | Do not follow. The report MUST list every live grant of the predecessor, each marked as not following
L579: Delegations the predecessor issued  | Evaluated against the predecessor's status; after termination they yield no ALLOW
L580: Budgets selected by the role  | Follow the role
L581: The predecessor's sessions  | Cease to authorize requests while the agent is inactive; credentials are not deleted and the epoch is not advanced

L583: 
L584: A conforming instantiation MUST support the queries in 【355†Table 14】, each answered from the captured history with evidence references and an explicit epistemic status: established from a verified replay, or not established and why.【356†¶】
L585: 【357†Table 14】: 【358†The four queries】
L586: Query  | Answers
L587: --- | ---
L588: WHY  | For a request: which grants, in which order, under which constraints, from which root, in which session and tenure
L589: RESPONSIBLE  | For an action: who is attributable at the time (actor, session, role, principal, mandator, authority source, controller) and who holds the duty afterwards. A statement about the records, not a legal judgment
L590: SURVIVES  | For an agent: lifecycle status, tenures, duties that outlive it, assignments, unresolved intents, reported outcomes, and authority dependencies its termination invalidates
L591: LINEAGE  | For an authority, admission or request: the capability roots and grant paths that support it, including required intersections and issuance authorizations, with any established human-lineage assessment. Confers no permission
L592: ### 【96†8.4.】 【97†Proof of Human Lineage】
L593: A PHL lineage query verifies recorded authority lineage and stated human-evidence predicates under selected policies. It MUST identify its selector, authenticated history identity, evaluated head and time, interpretation and assessment policies, disclosure scope and path-selection rule; an admission query MUST use the replay-reproduced decision path with all required intersections.
L594: The capability root is the root permission a path descends from; it is distinct from the history owner, the owner keys in force at the root-grant event and the grantor named there, and an answer MUST identify these separately. A valid owner signature on a grant establishes the recorded edge; it MUST NOT by itself be reported as human evidence for the grantor or grantee.【359†¶】
L595: For a root issued under several owner approvals the answer MUST distinguish (a) whether its actual counting quorum contains a qualifying human-attested credential, (b) whether every quorum permitted by its policy requires one, and (c) any assessment of the named grantor; "human-authorized capability root issuance" denotes (a), judged in the root-grant event's frozen context. Counting MUST use the policy in force before the event.
L596: A query MUST distinguish established-true, established-false and unknown; missing or withheld evidence MUST NOT be treated as non-human; verification MUST terminate within declared limits and report partial coverage; and for several roots the answer MUST name its quantifier and MUST distinguish alternative paths from required partner paths. An authority-only query MUST distinguish provenance and liveness from action-specific authorization, and each returned path MUST keep its own root and result.
L597: Per-edge assessments MUST carry evidence references and MUST distinguish assessment at the edge's event, at query time and as current risk; under the attested floor a lapsed class MUST be reported as lapsed, and later expiry or revocation MUST NOT silently rewrite an established event-time conclusion. An unknown required branch prevents an established-true all-required-roots conclusion; an established-false required branch can establish a false one despite another unknown branch.
L598: A limited or redacted view MUST NOT assert an exhaustive all-path or total-count conclusion. Invalid supplied evidence MUST be distinguished from evidence unavailability. Ordinary authority validity and PHL attestation assurance MUST be reported separately unless the selected authority profile makes the latter an acceptance condition.
L599: A human signature in one observed quorum MUST NOT establish proposition (b); a genesis key set MUST NOT be presented as an inferred root-grant signing quorum; actor binding MUST NOT be counted as an owner approval.
L600: Counts MUST state their unit, deduplicate exact credentials, exclude evidence-only vouchers (a human-associated credential count MUST include only credentials whose assessment is established and report counting-authorization and actor-binding sets separately, and a count under a uniqueness policy MUST name that policy's domain, issuer assumptions and incomplete coverage), and MUST NOT present distinct keys as distinct humans; absent an authenticated uniqueness policy, a distinct-human count is reported as not established.
L601: A declared HUMAN class or omitted-class default MUST NOT be reported as a verified assessment. Disclosure MAY hide identities through a reviewed selective-disclosure profile whose public proof binds the same predicate, scope and context.【360†¶】
L602: ### 【98†8.5.】 【99†Query scope and investigation】
L603: A query result MUST bind the exact domain, genesis identity, interpretation versions, disclosure scope, evaluated head and time, and MUST distinguish a replay-derived conclusion from unavailable evidence, unsupported interpretation or unverified freshness; missing evidence MUST NOT be relabeled as DENY, and a caller-supplied proof or serialized state MUST NOT acquire established status from matching metadata alone.
L604: A query about an earlier prefix MUST report whether the supplied history's head is the same prefix, a verified strict extension (later position and matching commitment) or unverified. A historical ALLOW remains an answer about that prefix; present consequential use requires a separate current authorization. Commitment integrity, inclusion, finality, availability, historical authorization, freshness and external outcome MUST be reported as distinct axes.
L605: A private or commitment-only deployment MUST NOT claim a publicly reconstructible undisclosed graph. Public reconstruction MUST require independently obtainable bodies, schemas, policies and opening material; an unexplained root alone is insufficient. An indexer, cache or explanation interface MUST NOT be accepted as an authority source because it displays the records.【361†¶】

Activation MUST identify one existing duty, its rules commitment, the activating actor and the prior head, and MUST NOT rewrite earlier meanings or grant general upgrade power; the profile MUST specify one-activation and compatibility rules, signer purposes, authority prerequisites and finite disposition and contest allowances.

L179: ## 1. Conventions and architecture
L180: 
L181: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY have the meanings in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174. Module versions for this draft are CORE 0.4, DISC 0.4, A2A 0.4, RT 0.4, VERIFY 0.4, COMM 0.1, CONF 0.4, and SCHEMA 0.4. A deployment MUST pin an immutable revision or digest for each implemented module and dependency. An absent profile is unsupported, not implicitly conforming.
L182: An owner authorizes policy and appoints a lifecycle controller. A registrar binds a dedicated wallet to an identity. A runtime executes agent reasoning; an isolated signer enforces policy. Providers sell resources; facilitators settle payments. A commerce service accepts work without holding the owner's or agent's keys. These roles MAY share infrastructure but MUST retain the authorization boundaries below.
L183: All operations affecting funds or state MUST be authenticated, replay protected, and durably journaled.
L184: Unless a field explicitly specifies another algorithm, digests are SHA-256 over raw artifact bytes or RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes for structured records, encoded as 0x-prefixed lowercase hex. A digest field does not itself prove authorship. Decimal-string uint256 values MUST be range checked against 2^256 - 1 after parsing.
L185: Origin fields MUST contain only scheme and authority, without paths, queries, fragments, or user information; remote endpoint URLs MUST reject user information and follow the binding's SSRF restrictions.
L186: A binding MUST specify its request/response encoding, error taxonomy, authentication, authority checks, operation lookup, finality rule, and version negotiation. No implementation MAY infer authorization from natural-language instructions, an unsigned descriptor, TLS alone, or possession of a task identifier.
L187: ## 2. ALP-CORE: lifecycle and economic authority
L188: ### 2.1 States and valid transitions
L189: State  | Meaning
L190: --- | ---
L191: DRAFT  | Local agent configuration exists; no delegated spending authority.
L192: PROVISIONED  | Dedicated wallet exists and the owner has explicitly approved policy.
L193: REGISTERED  | Finalized identity, verified wallet binding, and discoverable service descriptor exist.
L194: ACTIVE  | One runtime has current spend authority and a real self-funding cycle has succeeded.
L195: SUSPENDED  | New work and ordinary autonomous spending are disabled; identity persists.
L196: RETIRED  | Terminal identity state; authority revoked and obligations assigned for resolution.

L201:         PROVISIONED --> REGISTERED
L202:         REGISTERED --> ACTIVE

L210: 
L211: REGISTERED-to-SUSPENDED and REGISTERED-to-RETIRED explicitly support abandonment or revocation before first activation. DRAFT or PROVISIONED configurations MAY be locally abandoned after cleaning up any side effects; this is not on-chain retirement. If registration was partially completed, the existing identity MUST be reconciled and retired through the registered-state recovery path before abandonment is declared complete.
L212: A transition MUST use an operation identifier, expected current sequence, target state, evidence commitment, policy digest, and authority epoch. The controller MUST serialize competing transitions through compare-and-set. A failed attempt has an outcome in the journal; FAILED is not a lifecycle state. Partial execution MUST NOT authorize downstream behavior or be reported as a successful transition.
L213: ### 2.2 Transition preconditions
L214:   * DRAFT to PROVISIONED: Create a wallet dedicated to this agent. Inventory all spend paths. Obtain explicit owner approval of every policy field. Store keys in a signer-accessible secrets facility; model code MUST NOT access them. No spend authority is issued before approval.
L215:   * PROVISIONED to REGISTERED: Register or reconcile one identity; verify current ownership and dedicated-wallet control; publish the descriptor and required interfaces; commit a finalized lifecycle record. An advertised Commerce profile requires its pinned task contract. A Core-only agent MUST explicitly advertise that Commerce is unsupported.
L216:   * REGISTERED to ACTIVE: Deploy the verified artifact; confirm endpoint ownership and readiness; install one current authority epoch; perform and reconcile one actual payment on the declared self-funding rail, including provider credit; then commit ACTIVE. Payment during activation is permitted only under an owner-approved, bounded activation capability. New tasks remain disabled until activation commits.
L217:   * ACTIVE to SUSPENDED: Atomically stop new task acceptance and new ordinary signing. Trigger on owner instruction, policy breach, low balance, unverifiable identity, loss of authority lease, or failed reconciliation. The controller MUST record the cause. Safety shutdown takes effect even if recording the chain transition is unavailable; discovery MUST report unavailable rather than continuing to advertise verified ACTIVE.
L218:   * SUSPENDED to ACTIVE: Revalidate owner, wallet, policy, resources, artifact, endpoint, and outstanding authorizations. Obtain fresh owner approval after a policy or ownership change. Install a unique current authority epoch and prove funding readiness. Prior completed activation evidence MAY be reused only if its binding remains unchanged and live credit is verified; otherwise repeat the funding cycle.
L219:   * Any permitted state to RETIRED: Stop intake and ordinary signing; finalize the permanent retirement record; revoke all spend paths; invalidate or wait out outstanding authorizations; transfer unresolved commitments to their precommitted settlement path; destroy runtime secrets after revocation and required handover evidence is durable. Until all required steps complete, report retirement as pending and keep operational gates closed.
L220: Suspension and retirement do not cancel escrow terms. Restricted settlement capabilities MAY survive solely for existing obligations if separately owner-approved, bounded by job, asset, amount, expiry, and callable method, and incapable of accepting new tasks or refilling resources. Fully permissionless escrow refunds require no agent key. Destruction of a signing key MUST NOT strand obligations that require it; arrange delegated settlement before destruction.
L221: ### 2.3 Partial failures and journal
L222: 
L223: The journal MUST distinguish `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `reconciling`. It MUST record external transaction identifiers before retrying an uncertain operation. The same operation identifier and identical request MUST resolve to one logical result; reusing it with different contents MUST fail with `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Irreversible effects MUST be reconciled forward, not hidden by restoring a local snapshot.
L224: Partial failure  | Required behavior
L225: --- | ---
L226: Identity created, wallet binding fails  | Remain PROVISIONED, disable activation, record the identity, retry binding against that identity.
L227: Wallet binding succeeds, descriptor publication fails  | Keep spending and intake disabled; repair publication before REGISTERED.
L228: Registry checkpoint fails after publication  | Treat public descriptor as pending, not registered; reconcile chain state before retry.
L229: Deployment succeeds, readiness or payment fails  | Remain REGISTERED; disable ordinary authority; reconcile payment before retry.
L230: Payment settles, provider credit is unknown  | Hold reservation and reconcile with provider; do not automatically purchase again.
L231: ACTIVE checkpoint succeeds but response is lost  | Read committed state by identity and sequence; do not issue another authority lease.
L232: Process crashes mid-task  | Persist job ownership and committed terms; resume idempotently or follow timeout settlement.
L233: Retirement checkpoint succeeds, revocation is pending  | Registry stays terminal; advertise retirement cleanup pending and never restart work.
